title: Trust Portal: data provisioning playbook (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for packaging and delivering the minimal, repeatable dataset that customers request via the Trust Portal during security reviews. Focus is on: RBAC v2 role evidence, canonical audit-log export, SIEM-friendly delivery formats, and an automated evidence bundle that maps to common questionnaire items.

Audience:
- Security engineering and product security owners who validate customer requests
- Solutions engineers and CSMs preparing Trust Portal uploads
- Observability and infra teams responsible for log extraction and exports

Scope:
- Only covers data provisioning for customer questionnaires and Trust Portal uploads (not legal review or contractual items).
- Targets Hosted API and Dedicated telemetry; Private deployments require separate on-prem instructions (link to on-prem runbook in linked_artifacts).

High-level approach (summary):
1) Intake: customer selects requested artifacts in Trust Portal UI or via intake form (RBAC snapshot, audit-log slice, SIEM export, evidence manifest).
2) Verify: product-security reviews request scope and data retention constraints.
3) Extract: observability extracts RBAC role assignments and a time-bounded audit-log slice.
4) Normalize: convert events to JSONL and CEF/syslog as requested; obfuscate PII per policy.
5) Bundle: create evidence bundle with manifest, hashes, KMS-signed pointer, and delivery link.
6) Deliver: upload to Trust Portal and notify customer with ephemeral access.

RBAC v2 evidence checklist (what to include):
- Role model diagram snapshot (png) and brief narrative of role intent (string).
- Canonical role table CSV: role_id, role_name, permissions_count, permitted_resources_summary, inherited_roles, created_at.
- Current assignment export (JSONL): principal_id, principal_type (user/service), assigned_role_ids, assignment_ttl (if any), assignment_source (console/api/sync).
- Config hashes: sha256 of the RBAC policy blob and of the role-assignment export.
- Mapping to questionnaire items: map each role to common Q items (e.g., Q12: who can create API keys -> roles [platform_admin, infra_engineer]).

Audit log slice schema (recommended canonical export):
- Export format: newline-delimited JSON (JSONL) is preferred. Provide CEF/syslog as optional.
- Required event fields (one-per-line JSON object):
  - event_timestamp (ISO8601 UTC)
  - request_id (string, unique)
  - trace_id (string)
  - principal_id (string)
  - principal_type (user|service|external)
  - principal_roles (list of role_ids)
  - action (string, e.g., model.generate, token.create, config.update)
  - resource_type (string)
  - resource_id (string)
  - outcome (success|failure|denied)
  - http_status (int|null)
  - latency_ms (int)
  - model_name (string|null)
  - model_version (string|null)
  - quant_profile (string|null)
  - node_id (string|null)
  - client_ip (ip)
  - user_agent (string|null)
  - request_payload_hash (sha256|null)
  - response_size_bytes (int|null)
  - additional_metadata (freeform map)

Notes on the schema:
- Keep field set small and strongly typed. Avoid embedding unstructured blobs in the primary export unless absolutely required.
- For privacy, mask prompt text and any PII; surface a request_payload_hash so reviewers can correlate without exposing sensitive content.
- Include both request_id and trace_id to enable cross-service joins.

SIEM export options:
- JSONL (recommended): directly consumable, preserves schema above.
- CEF (ArcSight) flavor: map event fields to CEF header -> extension, include rt (event_timestamp), suser (principal_id), msg (action + resource), outcome in outcome extension.
- Syslog (RFC5424): for customers needing syslog ingestion, provide a forwarder config and a compressed tar.gz of syslog files for the window requested.
- Delivery: provide signed download URL(s) that expire (default 7 days). For sensitive customer on-site uploads, coordinate with their security contact.

Evidence automation flow (playbook for infra):
- Trigger: intake -> create JIRA ticket (SEC-TRUST-PORTAL-xxx) and a workspace in the evidence pipeline.
- Queries: pre-defined queries in our telemetry cluster for RBAC snapshot and audit-log slices (links in linked_artifacts).
- Sanitize: run PII redaction lambda that replaces prompt/string content with [REDACTED] and emits payload hash.
- Packaging: assemble files into a bundle: rbacs.csv, rbacs-assignments.jsonl, audit.jsonl (partitioned by day), manifest.json (list of files + sha256 + mapping to questionnaire items).
- Sign: sign manifest with KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:alias/trust-portal-signing (ops-only).
- Upload: push to trust-portal storage bucket with object ACL=private + signed URL.
- Notify: webhook to customer contact (or manual CSM email) with link and audit trail.

Manifest minimal fields (example line items shown in the manifest file):
- file_name, file_sha256, file_size_bytes, created_by, extracted_window_start, extracted_window_end, mapped_questions (comma separated), exposure_risk_level

Example manifest row (CSV friendly):
rbacs-assignments-2024-09-01.jsonl,9f2b...e3,12098,infra-service,2024-09-01T00:00:00Z,2024-09-07T23:59:59Z,Q3,Q5,LOW

Checklist for CSMs before delivery:
- Confirm exact scope with customer (time window, format, redaction rules).
- Confirm legal/contract constraints (retention or export restrictions).
- Confirm recipient identity and delivery channel.
- Run RBAC snapshot and compare to prior snapshot (note significant diffs in delivery notes).
- Attach manifest and KMS signature.

Small troubleshooting guide:
- If audit export is missing fields: verify telemetry pipeline version (tag) used for extraction and include tag in manifest.
- If customer rejects delivery for too much data: offer narrower window or field-level redaction and re-run pipeline.
- If SIEM ingest fails: provide JSONL + sample mapping file to customer SIEM team; include example CEF line for one event.

Unresolved questions (need product-security/infra alignment):
- Do we expose model prompts for debug with explicit customer consent, or always redact? (current default: redact, escalate only with approval).
- Standard TTL for signed URLs (7 days proposed) — ops to confirm acceptable SLAs.
- KMS key ownership and rotation cadence for manifest signing — security team to finalize.

Next steps / action owners in this WIP:
- Asha: finalize manifest field list and add example json manifest file (due 2024-10-05).
- Liam: add the RBAC snapshot query and an automated runner (POC) in infra (jira SEC-1267).
- Maya: draft customer-facing Trust Portal guidance text for choosing export formats and redaction options (link to draft in Confluence).
- Jordan: implement small shim to output CEF mapping for customers who request legacy SIEM format.

Appendix: quick references and links:
- Typical mapping of questionnaire items to artifacts: Q1 (Who has admin) -> rbacs.csv + assignments.jsonl; Q7 (audit retention) -> retention-policy doc; Q12 (key creation) -> key-audit-log slice.
- Slack threads: #trust-portal-deliveries (search: "RBAC snapshot delivery").
- Example JIRA: SEC-1299 (customer ACME export) contains a sample manifest and signed URL flow.

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep this playbook intentionally small — we will delegate complex scenarios to the Security-Assessment playbook.
- When packaging, avoid including raw prompt text by default.
- Build a small UI option in Trust Portal: "include prompts (requires approval)" so CSMs can capture explicit consent.
summary: Working playbook for extracting, normalizing, and delivering RBAC and audit evidence to customers via the Trust Portal. Focused on JSONL canonical schema, SIEM options, manifest + KMS signing, and an automation pipeline with owners.
